title: What Does the Bible Actually Say About Dating?
paragraphs:
What Does the Bible Actually Say About Dating?
The Question That Has Broken Hearts, Started Marriages, Destroyed Faith, and Left Millions Wondering If They Are Following God or Following Their Feelings
Nobody in the Bible ever asked Jesus, “Should I date him?”
Nobody walked up to Paul and said, “How long should we talk before becoming official?”
You will not find Abraham creating a dating profile.
You will not find Peter discussing relationship status updates.
You will not find a single verse that says, “Thou shalt date for six months before engagement.”
Yet every day millions of Christians wrestle with one of the most emotionally powerful questions of modern life:
What does God actually want from me when it comes to dating?
Because beneath every relationship question is a deeper spiritual question.
Can I trust God with my future?
Can someone like me—after all my mistakes, regrets, failed relationships, sexual sins, heartbreaks, compromises, and scandals—still experience God's best?
That question is where this journey begins.
"The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately sick; who can understand it?"
The Hebrew word translated "deceitful" is עָקֹב (aqov), carrying the idea of something crooked, twisted, or difficult to trace.
That is why dating becomes so confusing.
Yet none of those things are designed to be our compass.
Scripture never teaches believers to be led by feelings.
Scripture teaches believers to be led by God.
"Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding." (Proverbs 3:5)
One path leads to self-centered romance.
The other leads to Christ-centered relationships.
And that distinction matters more than most people realize.
Because dating is not primarily about finding the right person.
Dating is about becoming the right person under the lordship of Jesus Christ.
Because holiness rarely trends on social media.
Yet holiness is exactly what Scripture prioritizes.
When Paul wrote to believers struggling with sexual temptation, he said:
"For this is the will of God, your sanctification..." (1 Thessalonians 4:3)
The Greek word is ἁγιασμός (hagiasmos), meaning being set apart for God.
The phrase "sexual immorality" comes from the Greek word πορνεία (porneia).
It encompasses every sexual activity outside God's covenant design for marriage.
Not because God is trying to ruin relationships.
And the Creator always knows how His creation functions best.
The world sees boundaries as restrictions.
A river without banks becomes a flood.
Fire without a fireplace becomes destruction.
Love without God's design becomes chaos.
And many people reading this know exactly how painful that chaos can become.
Perhaps you gave your heart away too quickly.
Perhaps you compromised convictions to keep someone interested.
Perhaps you confused attention with love.
Perhaps you stayed because you feared being alone.
Perhaps you crossed boundaries you never thought you would cross.
Perhaps your story contains chapters you wish nobody knew.
But this is where the Gospel changes everything.
Because Christianity is not the story of perfect people finding perfect relationships.
Christianity is the story of sinners finding a perfect Savior.
One of the most remarkable truths in Scripture is that Jesus consistently moved toward scandalized people.
Toward those everyone else had already written off.
In John 8, religious leaders dragged a woman caught in adultery before Jesus.
"Neither do I condemn you; go, and from now on sin no more."
This is the heartbeat of the Gospel.
And it matters profoundly when discussing dating.
Because many Christians live trapped between two lies.
But your sin is not your identity.
But your past is not your future.
But they are not greater than the cross.
"There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus."
The Greek phrase οὐδὲν κατάκριμα (ouden katakrima) means none whatsoever.
Because Jesus absorbed the judgment we deserved.
That truth changes how we approach relationships.
Instead of dating from desperation, we date from security.
Instead of seeking someone to complete us, we recognize Christ is already enough.
Instead of demanding another person become our savior, we rest in the Savior we already have.
That is why the most important relationship advice in the Bible is not actually about dating.
"Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness..." (Matthew 6:33)
Everything else flows from that priority.
A healthy relationship cannot carry the weight of being your god.
When two believers pursue Christ together, something beautiful happens.
Their relationship stops revolving around themselves.
It begins revolving around God's glory.
And that is ultimately the biblical purpose of every relationship.
Ephesians 5 reveals that marriage itself exists to reflect the relationship between Christ and His Church.
In other words, even the greatest earthly love story points beyond itself.
The Bridegroom who pursued His Bride.
The Savior who gave Himself sacrificially.
The King who redeemed people stained by sin.
The Redeemer who transforms scandal into grace.
And perhaps that is the greatest lesson Scripture offers about dating.
One day every dating relationship ends.
One day every earthly marriage ends through death.
But the relationship Christ purchased through His blood lasts forever.
That reality changes how we date.
"How close can I get to sin without crossing the line?"
But a Christ-centered pursuit of holiness, wisdom, purity, sacrificial love, and God's glory.
And if you are currently carrying regret, shame, heartbreak, rejection, failure, or wounds from past relationships, hear this clearly:
The enemy says your mistakes are your identity.
Jesus says His grace is greater.
The enemy says your future is ruined.
The enemy says the scandal defines you.
Jesus says the cross defines you.
Because the Gospel has always been about God taking shattered lives and creating something beautiful.
Yet God rewrote every one of their stories.
Maybe that is why someone needed to read this today.
Not because you needed another dating article.
But because you needed to remember that Jesus has not given up on you.
And His power is still transforming lives.
Has your pursuit of relationships drawn you closer to Christ or farther from Him?
Has your desire for love strengthened your faith or replaced it?
Your testimony may be exactly what another struggling believer needs to read.
Because someone else's story of redemption may begin with something as simple as a shared article.
The heart you are waiting for was never meant to replace the Savior who already died for you.
